VibePascal v55 -- aarch64-linux native compiler (runs on ARM64 Linux, e.g. a
64-bit Raspberry Pi).  -FU/-FE output directories are created instead of
aborting the build.
Source commit: eae5d3e919 (merge of fix/output-dir-autocreate)
Compiler fix:  4d10b26fe772dfbd4992cbeb53f09028f7dfee4f
Parent release: v54 (b7d2d9676ecf1d7d8250cd460b9c48069920513e)
Built: 2026-09-10, cross-built on x86_64-linux via compiler/ppcrossa64
Binary: bin/ppca64  md5 7a41c2c459ebe303ecf47907d9e13f74

COMPILER BINARY ONLY.  Only compiler/options.pas changed between v54 and v55:
no RTL change, no package change, no PPU format change.  An existing v54 (or
v53/v52) aarch64-linux unit set stays valid, and the utility binaries are
unchanged and not re-shipped.

WHY THIS EXISTS
  -FE and -FU name where the COMPILER writes.  Up to and including v54 a
  missing one was an error: -FE reported 'Path "x/" does not exist' during
  option processing, and -FU failed later and far more obscurely at object
  write time ("Can't create assembler file: x/hello.s").  In both cases the
  compiler knew the path and made the user run mkdir.  v55 creates both
  directories up front, recursively.

  The fix shipped to Win64 first (2026-09-10) because that is where it was
  reported -- the Win64 package's bin/fpc.cfg carries -FU./units/$FPCTARGET,
  so the first compile after unpacking failed before the user had written a
  line of their own code.  Nothing about the behaviour was Windows-specific.
  This build carries the same fix to aarch64-linux.

  One behaviour change: -FE on a missing directory used to error and now
  creates it.  An IMPOSSIBLE path still stops the build with the same
  general_e_path_does_not_exist message -- it is now reported only after
  creation has been TRIED and FAILED, so it arrives early and names the
  directory rather than surfacing later as an assembler-file error.

VERIFIED ON THIS TARGET, UNDER EMULATION (qemu-user, 2026-09-10)
  A/B against the PUBLISHED pre-fix v54 aarch64 binary (md5
  5cc202e1ee758321f9fba15aa7fb8ba8, preserved from dist and re-run this
  cycle), same source, same options, same fresh directory, varying ONLY the
  compiler.  11 corners; every "must compile" corner had its emitted aarch64
  binary EXECUTED under qemu and required to print 42, not merely link:

    -FU one level deep .............. v54 fail (Can't create assembler file)  v55 pass
    -FU three levels deep ........... v54 fail                                v55 pass
    -FE relative .................... v54 fail (Path "od2/" does not exist)   v55 pass
    -FU and -FE together ............ v54 fail                                v55 pass
    -FU absolute .................... v54 fail                                v55 pass
    -FU units/sub ................... v54 fail                                v55 pass
    -FU on an EXISTING dir .......... v54 pass                                v55 pass
    no -FU/-FE at all ............... v54 pass                                v55 pass
    an fpc.cfg carrying
      -FU./units/$FPCTARGET ......... v54 fail (./units/aarch64-linux/)       v55 pass
    -FU under a PLAIN FILE .......... v54 refuse (1)                          v55 refuse (1)
    -FU under a READ-ONLY dir ....... v54 refuse (1)                          v55 refuse (1)

  BASELINE 4/11, FIXED 11/11.  The two must-refuse corners still refuse with a
  non-zero exit and no internal error on both compilers, so the check can
  still fail -- an all-pass harness would prove nothing.  Identical shape to
  the x86_64 result the fix commit records (4/11 -> 11/11).

  No semantic regression: tinlinevarnativeint1 (checks=45 fails=0,
  NativeInt=8) and the cy1096 block-scope finalization matrix (all corners
  released exactly once) were compiled AND run under qemu by BOTH the v54 and
  the v55 binary with byte-identical verdicts.

WHAT THIS IS NOT
  qemu-user is an emulator, not aarch64 hardware.  It runs the real shipped
  bytes and real aarch64 instruction encodings, so codegen and RTL defects do
  surface -- but nobody has yet run any VibePascal ARM artifact on physical
  ARM silicon, and this release does not change that.

REPRODUCE IT: dist/arm-runtime-proof.sh re-runs the published-byte checks from
a clean checkout.  It hash-checks each shipped compiler against the md5 in its
own VERSION.txt and refuses to continue on a mismatch, so a pass is a statement
about the published bytes rather than about a local rebuild.
